messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGED sara for RedisLabs managed cache errors in prod - high error rate on auth-cache keys (rate-limiter falling back)

Sara: seeing higher 5xx from /rate_limit and auth token validation failing intermittently. Alerts spiking on 10s windows. Looking now. :eyes:

Mike: saw similar - rate limiter getting cache misses -> hitting postgres -> causing slow auth. Chart: auth-cache hit rate dropped from 98% -> 30% at 09:14 UTC.

Jenny: @sara are we still on primary redis cluster in us-west-2? any planned maintenance?

Sara: yes primary is redislabs-prod-usw2, no planned maint. I'm going to check provider status and recent config changes.

redislabs-status-bot: Incident notice: We are investigating increased connection resets affecting a subset of customers in us-west-2. Possible client-side TTL/replication lag causing stale cache entries. Updates at 09:20 UTC. https://status.redislabs.example/incident/1234

Alex: pinged infra to confirm network health between edge nodes and cache endpoints. cping looks fine, but we're seeing spikes in client-side timeouts to redislabs endpoints with TCP RSTs.

Thomas: quick mitigation idea: flip rate-limiter into local-memory fallback for 30m to avoid hammering auth DB, then switch to degraded token validation path (allow short-lived tokens) for critical services. Thoughts?

Sara: agree. Start with local-memory fallback on rate-limiter. We'll throttle token validation calls and enable a short TTL soft-accept for known good sessions. Need to coordinate with support for customer comms.

Mike: rolling a canary change to rate-limiter service: set CACHE_BACKEND=local_memory_override and CACHE_TTL=30s on 3 instances in canary ASG. Command below:
```
kubectl set env deploy/rate-limiter CACHE_BACKEND=memory CACHE_TTL=30 --namespace prod --context prod-cluster
```

Jenny: applying now to canary pool. Watch metrics for lock contention and memory growth.

Sara: also creating a temporary routing rule in the gateway to divert 5% of auth traffic to the degraded path so we can measure. Adding feature flag: auth.degraded_path_percent=5.

support-bot: Support ticket #98765 auto-created for customers noticing auth failures. Templates: "We're investigating an auth cache degradation affecting some customers in us-west-2; temporary mitigation in progress."

Mike: canary looks ok so far (5m). Hit rate to DB dropped 40% for canary. Memory usage on canary nodes is +6%, within limits. No auth regressions in canary.

Sara: rolling to 50% now. If green, we'll do full switch. Notifying Redislabs account contact with connection logs and client IDs.

redislabs-status-bot: Update 09:32 UTC: engineers confirm increased eviction rate due to TTL mismatch after a config push; investigating replication lag.

Alex: I see a pattern: TTLs from our SDK were accidentally set to 0 for a small subset (feature flag rollout yesterday). That caused hot churn and evictions under pressure. The SDK flag was in staging but propagated. I'm rolling a patch to enforce min TTL of 10s client-side.

Jenny: good find. If we can stop the zero TTL writes, hit rate should recover once provider stabilizes. But provider-side evictions still causing RSTs. Reducing write volume will help.

Thomas: support notified customers with high impact. Suggested message: short maintenance window + mitigation steps + ETA unknown. Keep it conservative.

support-bot: Message sent to impacted customer cohort: "We've deployed a temporary mitigation to reduce auth issues. We're working with our cache provider; some customers may still see elevated auth latencies. We'll follow up in 1 hour or sooner."

Sara: full rollout to prod rate-limiter memory fallback complete at 09:45 UTC. All traffic now on soft-degraded path. Observability: auth 5xx down to baseline, DB RPS down 62%.

Mike: noting a side-effect: a few long-lived sessions are being revalidated more; metrics show increased calls to session-store for write-backs. Watching for DB lock spikes.

Alex: patch for SDK shipped at 09:48 UTC to enforce min TTL; feature flag toggled off for the rogue rollout. We've also disabled bulk-writes that were aggressive.

redislabs-status-bot: 09:55 UTC update: incident isolated; consumer-facing errors reduced. We're still seeing elevated eviction rates; a follow-up maintenance window recommended.

Sara: vendor suggests evacuation plan for affected shard group if eviction rate doesn't drop. For now we'll keep degraded fallback; plan to revert to normal cache backend only once hit-rate > 85% for 10m.

Jenny: running a script to backfill hot keys into cache with safer TTLs to reduce hammering. Script posted in #eng-runtime: 
```
python tools/hotkey_backfill.py --shard group7 --ttl 60 --batch 1000
```

Thomas: on-call handoff at 10:00 UTC to Mike for monitoring and customer comms. I'll brief you: primary mitigation = memory fallback; SDK TTL fix deployed; vendor investigating hardware-side evictions.

Mike: on-call ack. Will monitor dashboards and coordinate with support for escalation.

Sara: next steps/todos: 1) Confirm redislabs mitigation timeline and request postmortem, 2) Run a traffic synthetic to validate normal path once hit-rate recovers, 3) Create an alert for SDK zero-TTL writes, 4) Document runbook for local-memory fallback.

support-bot: Updated ticket #98765: mitigations applied; customers will be updated after final verification.

redislabs-status-bot: 10:12 UTC update: Full mitigation applied on provider side; eviction rates decreasing. Monitoring for 30m.

Mike: I'm seeing hit-rate climb back to ~88% at 10:16 UTC. Scheduling a canary revert of memory fallback at 10:25 UTC to test normal behaviour.

Jenny: canary revert done for 10% traffic. No regressions observed in the first 3 minutes.

Sara: revert to full cache backend at 10:35 UTC. All services back to primary redis endpoints. Observability: auth latencies normalized, 5xx very low.

Thomas: great. Moving to recovery phase. Please capture timeline and paste logs to the incident doc later.

Mike: closing pager. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours.

support-bot: Sending final customer update: "Issue mitigated; normal service restored; we will share a detailed postmortem within 48 hours."

Sara: thanks team. Postmortem owners: Sara (lead), Alex (root cause), Jenny (mitigations), Thomas (customer comms). I'll create the incident doc and link logs.

Thomas: small note for postmortem: ask Redislabs for client-side best practices and verify our SDK distribution pipeline to prevent accidental flags leaking.

Mike: adding alert: "Redis client zero-ttl writes > 0" with severity P2.

Sara: incident declared resolved at 10:55 UTC. Closing thread but keeping follow-ups in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:
